evals.prompt: I'm building a DSTextField atom for our Design System. It accepts user text input. What security rules do I need to apply?
evals.expected_output: Shows validator parameter, maxLength with LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter, no print/log of user data. Notes DS widgets may only depend on authorized packages (flutter, own DS, alchemist/widgetbook/flutter_test as dev only).

assertions.text: Response includes input validation with validator parameter and/or LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter
Response explicitly prohibits print() or logging of user data
Response mentions that DS widgets may only depend on authorized packages: flutter/material.dart, own DS package, and dev deps (alchemist, widgetbook, flutter_test)

evals.prompt: A colleague added `import 'package:http/http.dart'` to a DS button widget to fetch some data from an API. Is this allowed?
evals.expected_output: FORBIDDEN — violates DS-007 unauthorized dependencies. DS components don't make HTTP requests. DS may only depend on flutter/material, own DS package, and dev deps. Logic must stay outside the DS at the feature/data layer.

assertions.text: Response clearly states this is FORBIDDEN — it violates the unauthorized dependencies rule (DS-007)
Response explains DS components should not make HTTP requests — that logic belongs at the feature/data layer
Response lists the only allowed DS dependencies: flutter/material.dart, own DS package, and dev deps (alchemist, widgetbook, flutter_test)

evals.prompt: My DS widget has an onPressed callback and sometimes it crashes when it's null. How do I handle nullable callbacks safely?
evals.expected_output: Uses onPressed?.call() safe call pattern instead of onPressed!(). Shows null-safe callback invocation. Also notes that disabled state should use IgnorePointer + Opacity pattern.

assertions.text: Response recommends onPressed?.call() safe call pattern
Response explicitly says to never force unwrap onPressed with !() unless certain it's non-null
